hooks.text: Soviet reports claimed the first dog in orbit survived for days.
For 45 years, official records lied about Laika's spaceflight.
The first animal in orbit never had a chance of returning.

title: The 45-Year Cover-Up of Space Dog Laika
description: Soviet officials claimed Laika survived peacefully in orbit for days. In 2002, the tragic truth about her final hours was finally revealed.

beats.text: Soviet reports claimed the first dog in orbit survived for days.
beats.visual: photograph of Laika inside the Sputnik 2 capsule before flight, 1957

beats.text: Soviet engineers had rushed to assemble Sputnik 2 in under four weeks.
beats.visual: photograph of Nikita Khrushchev speaking at an official state event, 1957

beats.text: Trainers prepared Moscow stray Laika by confining her in shrinking cages for twenty days.
beats.visual: photograph of candidate dogs in Soviet space program training facilities, 1957

beats.text: Inside the tiny capsule, chains locked her so tightly she could not turn around.
beats.visual: schematic diagram of the internal cabin of Sputnik 2 capsule, 1957

beats.text: In weightlessness, medical sensors showed her heartbeat took three times longer to calm.
beats.visual: photograph of R-7 rocket launch at Baikonur Cosmodrome carrying Sputnik 2, 1957

beats.text: In 2002, mission scientist Dimitri Malashenkov finally revealed the truth.
beats.visual: photograph of the Conquerors of Space monument in Moscow, 1964
subjects: Monument to the Conquerors of Space
queries: Monument to the Conquerors of Space Moscow

beats.text: Thermal control failed, and Laika died from overheating and stress within seven hours.
beats.visual: illustration of Sputnik 2 in Earth orbit showing thermal control capsule components, 1957

beats.text: The empty spacecraft completed 2,570 orbits before burning up in Earth's atmosphere.
beats.visual: commemorative Soviet postage stamp featuring Laika and Sputnik 2, 1957

beats.text: For forty-five years, the world believed a carefully scripted myth.
beats.visual: photograph of Laika statue standing atop a rocket at a Moscow military research facility, 2008
